sources.title: Run vLLM in Spark
sources.summary: Long-running NVIDIA dev forum thread tracking vLLM build/run problems on DGX Spark (SM121/SM121a Blackwell target) around Oct 2025, with fixes landing over following weeks.

facts.claim: vLLM import fails with 'undefined symbol: _Z20cutlass_moe_mm_sm100' on DGX Spark; fix is a CMakeLists.txt patch excluding SM120/121 from CUDA 13 builds before compiling.
Triton 3.5.0 fails PTXAS on '.tile::gather4' for sm_121a; workaround is building Triton from the main branch instead of the pinned release.
PyTorch 2.9.0+cu130 officially lists CUDA capability support 8.0-12.0 while DGX Spark reports capability 12.1, producing a mismatch warning.

Working path: use NVIDIA's vLLM container tag 25.09-py3 and rebuild vLLM from source inside it, with env vars TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1a and TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas; gpt-oss-120b safetensors load took ~6:34 (total ~402s).

sources.relevance_to_us: Direct precedent for ch4/ch5: expect vLLM-on-Spark to need a source rebuild against the NVIDIA container base, not a pip install, and to hit SM121-specific kernel gaps — plan the inference-stack chapter around a known-good container tag rather than upstream vLLM releases.

sources.title: Inference best results on Spark - not llama.cpp not VLLM -> SGLang
sources.summary: Jan 10-11, 2026 forum comparison of SGLang vs llama.cpp vs vLLM on a single DGX Spark running GPT-OSS-120B (MXFP4), concluding SGLang edges out llama.cpp on this model but trails main-branch SGLang feature parity.

facts.claim: SGLang on GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4: ~51-52 tok/s across short/medium/long context (127/500/1000 tokens), about 13% faster than llama.cpp's 46 tok/s on the same model.
llama.cpp on GPT-OSS-20B reaches 61 tok/s (faster than the 120B MoE model as expected from fewer active params).
128K context for SGLang on this model needs 102GB GPU memory vs 88GB for 64K context, leaving only 12.8GB free vs 28.7GB — a hard ceiling on Spark's 128GB unified pool.
The DGX-Spark SGLang build in circulation is described as 'a single orphaned spark build... that lags behind the main branch'; vLLM performance on gpt-oss-120b is called 'a little disappointing'.

sources.relevance_to_us: Ch6/ch4 backbone number: on a single Spark, expect ~45-60 tok/s decode on a MoE 20B-120B class model regardless of engine, and budget unified-memory headroom carefully — 128K context alone can eat 100GB+.

sources.title: DGX Spark Playbooks Update - Jan 2026
sources.summary: NVIDIA-authored (margaretz) Jan 21, 2026 post announcing new/updated official DGX Spark Playbooks post-CES: TensorRT-LLM two-Spark workflow improvements, EAGLE-3 speculative decoding for GPT-OSS-120B, and 7 new playbooks including Nemotron 3 Nano, Live VLM WebUI, Isaac Sim/Lab, SGLang & vLLM support matrices, and two-Spark PyTorch fine-tuning up to 70B via FSDP+LoRA.

facts.claim: New playbook: 'Fine-tune with PyTorch' supports distributed fine-tuning across two DGX Spark systems for LLMs up to 70B parameters using FSDP and LoRA.
New playbook: 'Nemotron 3 Nano', a 30B-parameter MoE model, added for local LLM experimentation.
Speculative decoding playbook updated with a new EAGLE-3 example demonstrating GPT-OSS-120B inference.
Feedback channel given as spark-playbook-feedback@nvidia.com, posted by NVIDIA staff account margaretz.

sources.relevance_to_us: These are the exact official playbooks the DGX Spark chapters (ch2/ch4/ch5/ch11) should point readers at instead of re-deriving setup steps; the two-Spark FSDP+LoRA playbook is a ready template for ch22 scale-out and ch6 fine-tuning coverage.

sources.title: DGX Spark / GB10 forum category listing
sources.summary: Category sweep surfacing the highest-traffic and highest-signal threads on the DGX Spark board: large community benchmark threads, a third-party throughput tool (veloGB10), and hardware failure/thermal threads.

facts.claim: veloGB10 v0.4.0 release thread reports Qwen 3.8-27B code-gen sustained throughput scaling with Spark count: 125 tok/s at 4x, 85 tok/s at 2x, 75 tok/s at 1x.
A DeepSeek-V4-Flash single-Spark thread reports 1,000 tok/s prefill and 59 tok/s multi-agent serving throughput on one unit.
A hardware-failure thread reports 2 DGX Spark Founders Edition units RMA'd within 48 hours after silent hard-locks under sustained inference load.

A community thread documents a custom 'screwless, modular' dual-Spark cooling cage using three 120mm fans, plus separate fan-control and PXE-recovery-failure threads (recovery images 1.145.33 / 1.135.29 failing) and a kernel-panic-after-update thread.

sources.relevance_to_us: Thermal/RMA and PXE/kernel-panic threads are directly relevant to ch1/ch2/ch14 (day-1 setup and observability should flag sustained-load stability as a known risk, not assume it's solved); the veloGB10 scaling numbers (125/85/75 tok/s at 4x/2x/1x) are a citable multi-Spark scaling curve for ch22.

sources.title: llama.cpp DGX Spark performance discussion
sources.summary: GitHub Discussions thread on the llama.cpp repo collecting community DGX Spark benchmark numbers across multiple quantized MoE and dense models, plus cross-platform comparisons.

facts.claim: GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4 MoE on DGX Spark via llama.cpp: ~1,956 t/s prefill (2048 tok), ~60.6 t/s generation (32 tok), dropping to ~40.6 t/s generation at 32K context depth.
Qwen3 Coder 30B A3B Q8_0 on DGX Spark: ~1,654 t/s prefill, ~44.3 t/s generation.
GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 MoE on DGX Spark: ~2,009 t/s prefill, ~60.9 t/s generation.
AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo) comparison point: ~47.5 t/s generation on the same model, with much faster load time (~25s vs DGX Spark's 1+ minutes on older kernels, ~22s once kernel-optimized).

sources.relevance_to_us: Canonical llama.cpp numbers for ch4/ch6 comparison tables; the load-time-depends-on-kernel-version finding matters for ch2 day-1 DGX OS setup guidance (recommend checking/updating kernel before benchmarking).

sources.title: Introducing the Spark Arena
sources.summary: Feb 11, 2026 launch post for Spark Arena (spark-arena.com), a community-built reproducible LLM benchmark leaderboard for DGX Spark, created by forum members Raphael Amorim and eugr, integrating with their existing spark-vllm-docker and llama-benchy tools.

facts.claim: Spark Arena launched Feb 11, 2026 to fix 'lack of reproducibility and indexing' of scattered DGX Spark benchmark experiments; captures full CLI flags, quantization, backend, and node topology per submission.

Built by forum community members Raphael Amorim and eugr (eugr is also the author of spark-vllm-docker and llama-benchy, both referenced repeatedly across other DGX Spark threads as the de facto community vLLM build path).

sources.relevance_to_us: spark-vllm-docker (github.com/eugr/spark-vllm-docker) and spark-arena.com are candidate concrete citations/tools for ch4/ch5 (inference stacks) and a good pointer for ch16's local validation-loop chapter (borrow their reproducible-recipe format for our own agentic test harness).

sources.title: I am EXTREMely disappointed with the current state of DGX Spark
sources.summary: April 3-5, 2026 thread airing real-owner frustration: gap between FP4/NVFP4 marketing and delivered software maturity, multi-node deployment failures, repeated OS reinstalls, ConnectX-7 kernel issues, and USB/RAM stability bugs — with community members (notably eugr) posting concrete fixes and workarounds.

facts.claim: User parad8x010 (Apr 3, 2026): 'key capabilities were promoted before they were fully ready' — NVFP4 immature/inconsistent, requiring workarounds.
User Digital_David (Apr 3, 2026) reports OpenClaw/Nemotron-3-Super on DGX Spark: 3-minute initial load, 1-3 minute response times, ~15 t/s, and crashes.
User jonasbridelu (Apr 4, 2026): 'I have formatted my DGX for the third time' due to ConnectX-7 incompatibility and kernel support gaps.

Community fix (eugr, Apr 4-5, 2026): FP8 kernel gaps on SM121 fixed in the latest spark-vllm-docker builds, with active NVFP4 support work ongoing; user sesmanovic reports a working setup running Qwen 3.5 35B generating 1M tokens/day.

sources.relevance_to_us: Important counterweight for ch3/ch4: as of April 2026, ConnectX-7 kernel compatibility and NVFP4 maturity were still live pain points months post-launch — the guide should recommend pinning to spark-vllm-docker/community-patched builds rather than stock releases, and flag USB/RAM stability under high GPU utilization as a thing to watch in ch14.

sources.title: 6x Spark setup
sources.summary: Dec 12-18, 2025 build log from user ericlewis777 scaling a DGX Spark cluster from 4 to 6 nodes over InfiniBand (MikroTik CRS812 DDQ switch with 400->200Gbps splitters), with NanoChat pretraining and tensor-parallel inference benchmarks across the cluster.

facts.claim: 6-node NanoChat (560M param) pretraining peaked at ~100,000 tok/s (batch size 32, 5.9% MFU); batch 21 gave ~99,000 tok/s (5.8% MFU), batch 40 dropped to ~89,500 tok/s.

4-node tensor-parallel inference: GPT-OSS-20B reached 9,000 tok/s total at 100 concurrent requests (41ms TTFT); GPT-OSS-120B reached 4,700 tok/s total at 100 concurrent (37ms TTFT); Qwen3-VL-32B-FP8 reached 3,000 tok/s total at 100 concurrent.
GLM-4.6-FP8 showed severe latency degradation at scale: 38-second time-to-first-token at 100 concurrent requests.
'Only pipeline parallelism works on most models' — tensor parallelism was limited/unreliable across nodes at this cluster size in Dec 2025; InfiniBand training traffic peaked at 24.6 Gbps (bursty).

sources.relevance_to_us: Best available real multi-node scaling data point for ch22 (multi-Spark scale-out): concurrent-request throughput and TTFT figures per model size, and the pipeline-vs-tensor-parallelism caveat should directly inform how we architect any multi-Spark demo.

sources.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark: great hardware, early days for the ecosystem
sources.summary: Simon Willison's Oct 14-15, 2025 hands-on review: praised hardware/docs, flagged ARM64 CUDA ecosystem immaturity (missing PyTorch 2.8 wheels) at launch, but noted rapid day-1 improvement as Ollama/llama.cpp/LM Studio/vLLM all shipped compatible builds within 24 hours of embargo lift.

facts.claim: DGX Spark specs per Willison: 128GB unified memory, 20 ARM64 CPU cores, GB10 Blackwell GPU with 119.68GB of that memory addressable to the GPU.
Georgi Gerganov's llama.cpp benchmarks on GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4: ~3,600 tok/s prompt processing, ~59 tok/s generation; GLM-4.5-Air-GGUF: ~817 tok/s prompt processing, ~18 tok/s generation.
At launch, 'CUDA on ARM64' was poorly documented with missing PyTorch 2.8 wheels; most existing ML tooling assumed x86, causing friction.

sources.relevance_to_us: Good ch2/ch4 narrative anchor for 'day-1 experience' — cite as the baseline the guide should show has since improved (contrast with the Jan 2026 2.5x speedup claim and later community fixes).

sources.title: Nvidia says it's more than doubled the DGX Spark's performance since launch
sources.summary: The Register's Jan 5, 2026 CES coverage of NVIDIA's claimed 2.5x average performance gain since October 2025 launch, driven by software (TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp, PyTorch) improvements concentrated in the prefill/compute-bound phase rather than memory-bandwidth-bound decode.

facts.claim: NVIDIA claims DGX Spark is '2.5x faster on average' since its October 2025 launch, announced at CES on Jan 5, 2026.

Gains are primarily software-driven (TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp, PyTorch updates) and concentrated in compute-bound work (prefill, fine-tuning, image/video gen); token-generation (decode) remains memory-bandwidth-limited and does not see comparable speedup.
The Register states it had not independently verified NVIDIA's 2.5x claim at time of publication.

sources.relevance_to_us: Important framing for ch1/ch6: the 273GB/s memory-bandwidth ceiling is a hard physical limit that software updates cannot fix for decode throughput — set reader expectations accordingly, distinguish prefill-bound vs decode-bound workloads in demos.

sources.title: Successful 2 DGX Spark cluster setup?
sources.summary: Oct-Dec 2025 thread walking through connecting two DGX Sparks via the official dgx-spark-playbooks repo: NCCL/UCX env vars, RoCE for GPU-to-GPU transfer, and a real gotcha (an IP-address typo causing SSH auth failures that looked like an NCCL bug).

facts.claim: Working NCCL/UCX config: export UCX_NET_DEVICES=enp1s0f0np0, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp1s0f0np0, OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=enp1s0f0np0.
'Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified' NCCL error traced to a typo'd IP octet ('1169' instead of '169') causing SSH timeout, not an actual NCCL/driver bug.
The discover-sparks helper script and cluster setup process come from cloning NVIDIA's official dgx-spark-playbooks GitHub repo, not a pre-installed tool.

sources.relevance_to_us: Concrete env-var recipe and a real debugging trap for ch3/ch22 two-Spark clustering instructions.

sources.title: How to run GLM-4.7 on dual DGX Sparks with vLLM (MoE support in spark-vllm-docker)
sources.summary: Thread on running large MoE models (GLM-4.6V, GLM-4.7-FP8 355B) across multi-Spark clusters via the community spark-vllm-docker project; notes tensor-parallel instability at 2-node scale and that GLM-4.7-FP8 (355B MoE) has been run on 4x Spark with SGLang + EAGLE speculative decoding.

facts.claim: GLM-4.7-FP8 (355B parameter MoE) has been run on a 4x DGX Spark cluster using SGLang with EAGLE speculative decoding.
Reported instability: 'Two-Spark cluster with vLLM using tensor-parallel-size 2 causes one node to drop while the other's GPU goes 100% forever.'
Community framing: without pairing two Sparks over InfiniBand you are 'wasting' the ConnectX-7 module each unit ships with, since single-Spark use leaves it idle.

sources.relevance_to_us: ch22 should flag vLLM tensor-parallel-size 2 as a known-unstable path on Spark clusters as of this thread; SGLang+EAGLE on 4x Spark is the better-attested path for large MoE models like GLM-4.7.

load_bearing_claims.claim: Single-Spark decode throughput on a 20B-120B MoE model sits in roughly the 45-61 tok/s band across llama.cpp/SGLang engines — this is the realistic per-unit number the guide should quote, not headline TFLOPS.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Sets reader expectations correctly for ch4/ch6 and prevents overselling DGX Spark as a datacenter-GPU substitute for interactive chat workloads.

load_bearing_claims.claim: NVIDIA's own Jan 2026 CES claim of a 2.5x average speedup since October launch applies to compute-bound phases (prefill, fine-tuning) and explicitly does NOT apply to memory-bandwidth-bound decode/token-generation.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Prevents the guide from citing a headline 2.5x number in a decode-throughput context where it doesn't apply — a common misreading risk for ch1/ch6.

load_bearing_claims.claim: As late as April 2026 (6 months post-launch), real owners were still reporting ConnectX-7/kernel incompatibilities requiring multiple OS reinstalls, and NVFP4 support was still described as immature by community experts.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Directly informs ch3 (joining the LAN / networking hardware) risk callouts and argues for pinning to community-patched builds (spark-vllm-docker) rather than stock software in ch4/ch5.

load_bearing_claims.claim: vLLM tensor-parallel-size 2 across a two-Spark cluster is reported as unstable (one node drops, other GPU pins at 100%), while pipeline parallelism and SGLang+EAGLE speculative decoding on 4x Spark are the better-attested multi-node paths for large MoE models.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Directly shapes what parallelism strategy ch22's multi-Spark scale-out chapter should recommend/demo — avoid vLLM TP=2 as a headline example.
